summary: Concurrent transmit paths inspect and update txq->xmit_lock_owner while deciding whether to take the per-queue transmit lock.

call_chain.evidence: KCSAN write stack reports __dev_queue_xmit and dev.ll defines it.
Inline helper writes txq->xmit_lock_owner = -1 before spin_unlock.
KCSAN read stack reports another interrupt context in __dev_queue_xmit.

interleaving: One softirq transmit path owns a netdev queue and clears xmit_lock_owner during unlock.
Another transmit path tests txq->xmit_lock_owner to decide whether it already owns the queue.
The fix marks both lock-owner writes and the unlocked read with READ_ONCE/WRITE_ONCE.

ground_truth_access.required_ordering: Transmit queue owner checks must tolerate concurrent lock/unlock owner updates and use marked accesses.

vulnerability_surface.why_relevant: xmit_lock_owner records which CPU owns the transmit queue lock and is intentionally sampled outside the same synchronization as the writer.

aliases.name: txq->xmit_lock_owner
aliases.evidence: txq is the selected transmit queue for the skb.

aliases.name: txq->xmit_lock_owner
aliases.evidence: Inline unlock helper clears the owner field.

aliases.name: queue->xmit_lock_owner
aliases.evidence: Queue initialization sets the field to -1.

thread_a.evidence: HARD_TX_UNLOCK expands to __netif_tx_unlock for the same queue.

thread_b.evidence: __dev_queue_xmit reads the owner before deciding whether to take HARD_TX_LOCK.

allocated_by: netdev queue allocation during net_device setup

coverage.analysis_conclusion: The patched field access is in __dev_queue_xmit and inline netdevice helpers; caller stack files are candidate context only.

patch_hunks: 7a10d8c810cf annotates xmit_lock_owner writes in include/linux/netdevice.h and the read in __dev_queue_xmit.
indirect_edges: HARD_TX_LOCK/HARD_TX_UNLOCK macros in include/linux/netdevice.h connect __dev_queue_xmit to the inline owner writes.
